newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy metal employers head rejects govt wage plan.
newsitem.headline: Italy metal employers head rejects govt wage plan.

text.p: The head of the Italian engineering employers' association, Gabriele Albertini, said on Tuesday that he opposed a government proposal for a new wage accord but was ready to resume talks with metalworkers' unions.
The head of Finmeccanica told a news conference in Milan: "We confirm our 'no' to the government but also our willingness to pursue the negotiations."

Albertini, who said the government's proposals were inflationary, added: "We want to continue with the negotiation because this can reduce the difference between the gross cost for companies and net pay in workers' wage packets."
In a bid to break the stalement between employers and unions, the government has proposed that workers should be given a 200,000 lire a month pay rise to cover the 1996-98 contract period.

The previous two-year contract expired in June and unions are pressing for a wage raise to compensate for higher-than-expected inflation over the past two years which they say has eroded take-home pay.

Italian union leaders were meeting on Tuesday evening and could decide to call a general strike, union sources said. Unions have already staged several hours of strikes across the country to back their claims.
Labour Minister Tiziano Treu will preside over talks between employers and unions which are due to resume in Rome on Wednesday. Milan newsroom +392-66102321
